research_question: Can the frozen G1→G4 structural gate chain contract mechanism-candidate space while preserving the independently identified viable mechanism basin structure and its geometry?

transition_from_v002.reason: candidate-level target recall on design-only seeds was approximately 0.147–0.153, showing that candidate identity was the wrong preservation unit for the LII→LIII calibration
transition_from_v002.frozen_change: replace candidate-level recall as the primary preservation unit with basin/class preservation; G1→G4 and the independent viability oracle remain unchanged

gates.G3: has_bifurcation and soft-band temporal coherence with s_lo=0.08, s_hi=0.10, T_min=0.70

basin_definition.note: port of Chamber LIII clusterResiduals ordering and density rule

primary_preservation_requirements.signature_stratum_definition: (regime_base, family, composition) among target-positive candidates with baseline count >= 20

nulls.purpose: test whether basin preservation is specific to the structural gate or expected from generic pruning at the same survivor rate

decision_levels.LEVEL_A: basin/class geometry preserved with positive candidate reduction
decision_levels.LEVEL_B: LEVEL_A plus structural filter outperforms rate-matched random pruning on preregistered preservation metrics
decision_levels.LEVEL_C: LEVEL_A plus net end-to-end computational gain; complexity-class claims are out of scope

upi: blinded; not used for pruning or target/basin definition
